newsitem.title: UK: "My Fair Lady" royalties dispute settled.
newsitem.headline: "My Fair Lady" royalties dispute settled.

text.p: Two museums and a leading British stage school were set to receive a $2 million handout on Wednesday after a long-running dispute over royalties from the musical "My Fair Lady" was settled.

Lawyers for The British Museum, The Royal Academy of Dramatic Arts and the National Gallery of Ireland said they were "well satisfied" after a confidential agreement was reached with U.S. broadcasting group CBS.

They were the chief beneficiaries under the will of George Bernard Shaw, whose play "Pygmalion" was the basis for the musical that was a international stage success before being turned into a hit film.

Lawyers told the High Court in London that all difficulties had now been settled. The three beneficiaries stand to gain from an immediate payment of $2 million and an important source of income through to the next century.

"An important income stream, for the three has now been secured. Changes in the law have extended Shaw's copywright from the end of the year 2000 to the end of 2020," lawyer David Wills told reporters afterwards.
